newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili quickens pace as heads for Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili quickens pace as heads for Cuba.

text.p: Hurricane Lili picked up forward speed as it moved through the northwestern Caribbean toward Cuba Thursday, threatening the island with torrential rains and flooding, National Hurricane Center said.
At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the center of Lili was at latitude 19.9 north, longitude 83.2 west, about 230 miles (370 km) south-southwest of Havana.
The storm, packing winds of 75 mph (120 kph), was moving north-northeast at about nine mph (15 kph) and was expected to continue on that track for the next 24 hours.
Cuba's government extended a hurricane warning to cover the Isle of Youth and the mainland from Camaguey province westward, according to the hurricane center.
A tropical storm warning and hurricane watch remained in effect for the Cayman Islands. Forecasters said alerts could be issued for the Florida Keys and parts of the Bahamas later Thursday.
On its current track, the center of Lili was expected to approach the south Cuba coast late Thursday or early Friday.
Hurricane-force winds extended 25 miles (40 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended outward up to 140 miles (220 km).
Rainfall up to 12 inches (30 cm) was likely over Cuba, the Cayman Islands and parts of Central America, raising the possibility of deadly flash floods and mud slides in mountainous areas.
Storm surge flooding of three to six feet (1-2 meters) was possible near where the storm crosses mainland Cuba, forecasters said.
Rainbands from the storm were spreading over the islands and into the Florida Straits. Forecasters warned boaters in the Florida Keys to stay in port.
